title: String Quartet No. 5 · I. Allegro
subtitle: Sz. 102 / BB 110 · Thematic form
form: Sonata form with reversed and inverted thematic return

analysis.description: Thematic regions from Bartók’s formal outline, reproduced and discussed by Somfai (2021), with rehearsal markers located in the historical score. Three family rows show the reverse order and inversion of themes at their return. This is a formal map, not a catalogue of instrumental entries or every motivic recurrence. The development and coda are shown as formal sections without inventing internal theme occurrences.

entries.label: Appendix
entries.notes: Appendix to the first theme, A–B. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Transition
entries.notes: Transitional region B through m. 36, ending at the m. 37 downbeat. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Allusion
entries.notes: Allusion to the first theme, m. 37–C. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Lyrical theme
entries.notes: Lyrical theme at the end of the exposition, C–D. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Inversion
entries.notes: First theme in inversion, F–G; Bartók also permits F as an alternative beginning of the recapitulation. The outline's E denotes the region's tonality, not the first melodic pitch. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Inversion
entries.notes: Inverted lyrical theme, G–H: first of the reversed thematic regions in the principal recapitulation reading. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Inversion
entries.notes: Inverted transitional region, H–I. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

entries.label: Inversion
entries.notes: Inverted first-theme region, I–J; Bartók also permits I as an alternative beginning of the coda. Bounds are formal section boundaries, including initial rests where present; they do not measure a single subject statement or final-note release. The lane denotes a thematic family, not an instrument.

verification.method: YouTube watch-page metadata verified the work, movement, performer, Topic channel and label credit; playability OK and embedding allowed on the checked date. Musical timing was not measured.

notes: Only movement I is represented. Every duration uses quarter-note units, including the changing notated meters. Numbered measures follow the score; dotted local pulse guides are not counted as new measures.

Bartók’s outline calls the lyrical theme the second theme and the preceding contrasting region a transition. The three families here use descriptive names to avoid confusing that terminology with Ligeti’s three-theme account.
The principal reading places recapitulation at G and coda at J. Bartók explicitly allows F and I as alternative boundaries; the map preserves that ambiguity in the affected regions' notes.

The returned regions occur in reverse family order and inversion. This does not mean a literal note-by-note retrograde of the exposition. Blank family lanes do not imply silence or absence of related material.
